newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end ahead but shy from day's peaks.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end ahead but shy from day's peaks.

text.p: Italian stocks rowed back from earlier gains by the market's close on Wednesday, with the main indices standing 1.5 to 1.7 percent higher at the finish.
Turnover reached a massive 3.0 trillion lire ($1.69 billion) in hectic trade, according to preliminary stock market figures.
Dealers said orders for Italian blue-chips had rained down from abroad and from fund investors, with liquidity coming out of fixed income markets and flowing into equities.
Some said however the market was now ripening for a correction after recent gains.
The blue-chip Mib30 index ended 1.76 percent up at 23,100 after charging to a fresh all-time high of 23,517 in afternoon trade following a firm start on Wall Street.
The all-share Mibtel index also carved a new peak at 15,393 before ending only 1.57 percent higher at 15,163 as U.S. stocks then recoiled .
On individual stocks, dairy products group Parmalat was heavily sought and at one point stood around eight percent up.
It closed 5.3 percent higher at 2,662 lire with 24 million shares traded. Traders said it was in part playing catch-up with the market after lagging behind in recent days.
Other gainers included investment bank IMI which ended 7.11 percent higher at 18,006 having touched 18,490 earlier.

State-controlled Telecom Italia, the telecom giant resulting from the merger of Stet and Telecom Italia, also ranked among the top gainers of the day, ending 3.24 percent up at 6,185 after touching 6,310.
